newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo oil product market calm after New Year break.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo oil product market calm after New Year break.

text.p: The Tokyo oil products market was virtually deserted on Monday with most traders just returning from week-long New Year holidays, traders said.
"Today was the day for oil dealers to bring themselves up to speed after a long vacation," one trader said.

Open-spec naphtha for first-half March was assessed at $243.00/$244.50 per tonne. It was quoted at $239.00/240.50 on the last trading day before the New Year holidays. Second-half March was indicated at $240.50/242.00 in Monday trading.
In spreads, first-half March/first-half April was offered at plus $6.50, with no bids having emerged.
A fire broke out at a 40,000 barrel-per-day fuel oil desulphurisation unit at Tohoku Oil's Sendai refinery in northern Japan's Miyagi prefecture in Monday afternoon.

It is unclear whether the firm will seek spot cargoes to make up for expected losses in production, a spokeswoman said. The 100,000 barrel-per-day crude distillation unit and most secondary units at the plant are operating despite the fire. In middle distillates, domestic kerosene demand in December was estimated to have fallen by about 10 percent, or by 500,000 kilolitres, from a year ago amid relatively mild weather, traders said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
